title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is item 5)-6) of Grothendieck's 1965 notes on the motivic Galois group. On the previous pages, 4) introduced a conjecture he calls 'du double vaisseau' (the reading of 'vaisseau' is uncertain). It concerns k algebraic over Q (e.g. k = Qbar). It says that a motive M over k is faithfully captured by its 'double vessel': the Q-structure T_B(M), the k-structure T_DR(M), and the comparison isomorphism T_B ⊗ C ≅ T_DR ⊗_k C. Concretely, Hom(1,M) ⊗ Q is the set of classes lying in T_B ∩ T_DR; equivalently, the realization functor Mot(k) → {(V_Q, W_k, V⊗C ≅ W⊗C)} is fully faithful. The previous page tests this group-theoretically. It uses Vbar = V ⊗ Qbar, the stabilizers G_x and the closure of the torsor-type set {s^{-1}t}, and asks when V ∩ g(Vbar) recovers V^G. Item 5) notes that for k transcendental over Q this pointwise data is useless ('idiot!').

This page.
(i) For k an arbitrary algebraically closed field (embedded in C), Grothendieck still hopes that the functor (9.2) is fully faithful. (9.2) is probably the realization functor to Hodge-type or realization data. He reduces this (reading uncertain) to the case k = C. He says it would follow from three ingredients: the double-vaisseau conjecture of 4), plus the Tate or Hodge conjecture, plus a family statement 6).
(ii) Item 6). Let S be of finite type over a number field or Qbar. A motive over the function field k(S) spreads out over S. Consider the realization functors of 3), but without the Hodge filtration on T_DR(M). The target is triples: a Q-local system T_B on S(C), an algebraic vector bundle with integrable (Gauss-Manin) connection T_DR on S defined over the number field, and a comparison isomorphism (Riemann-Hilbert). The margin note 'vaisseau + connexion' = bundle + connection supports this reading. The double-vaisseau conjecture should imply this functor is fully faithful.
(iii) NB: when S is the spectrum of a number field, statement 6) is literally the double-vaisseau statement.

Problem served. The goal is to state a period-type full-faithfulness conjecture for motives over fields of arbitrary transcendence degree. The pointwise Betti/de Rham comparison is replaced by a relative comparison over a model S, with algebraic flat connections defined over Qbar. The absolute case is recovered at Qbar-points.
errors: The deduction 'double vaisseau ⟹ 6)' is not immediate. A horizontal compatible section over S specializes, at a Qbar-point s, to a Betti-de Rham class. By double vaisseau that class is motivic at s. One then still needs it to spread to a motivic class over the generic point. That is a variational Hodge/Tate-type statement (algebraic at one fibre plus flat ⟹ algebraic on all fibres). Grothendieck may be invoking 'Tate ou Hodge' for this, but the page does not make the step explicit.

The phrase 'sans filtration' matters. Dropping the Hodge filtration is consistent because full faithfulness is claimed for the Q-bar algebraic connection plus the Q-local system. Still, the precise target category of (9.2) is not recoverable from this page.

ideas.what: Conjecture 'du double vaisseau': for k ⊂ Qbar, motivic classes are exactly those in T_B ∩ T_DR(k); Mot(k) → (Betti Q-structure, de Rham k-structure, comparison) is fully faithful
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck period conjecture (de Rham-Betti / 'Grothendieck classes' form); full faithfulness to de Rham-Betti structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (via Lang 1966 footnote; André 1989/2004; Bost-Charles 2016; Kontsevich-Zagier 2001 for periods)
ideas.where_published: Not under this name; the period conjecture is attributed to Grothendieck via Lang's 'Introduction to transcendental numbers' and André's book

ideas.what: Family version: for S of finite type over a number field, the realization functor to (Q-local system on S(C), algebraic flat bundle on S over Qbar, comparison iso), without Hodge filtration, should be fully faithful
ideas.modern_name: Relative / families version of the period conjecture; de Rham-Betti structures over a base; relative period conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: André (motivic Galois groups in families, 1990s-2000s); Ayoub's relative Kontsevich-Zagier conjecture (Annals 2015); Bost-Charles

ideas.what: Reduction of full faithfulness over an arbitrary algebraically closed k (via k = C) to: double vaisseau at Qbar-points + Hodge/Tate + the family statement, by spreading out over a model S
ideas.modern_name: Spreading-out / specialization argument combined with variational Hodge conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard technique; variational Hodge conjecture attributed to Grothendieck (1966, de Rham cohomology paper, footnote)
ideas.where_published: Variational Hodge conjecture: footnote in 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, already in 1965, a relative version of his period ('double vaisseau') conjecture. For S of finite type over a number field, motives over S should be faithfully detected by the triple (local system, algebraic integrable connection over Qbar, Riemann-Hilbert comparison), with the Hodge filtration dropped. The absolute conjecture is recovered at S = Spec(number field). This anticipates the 'relative period conjecture' (Ayoub) and de Rham-Betti structures in families (André, Bost-Charles), which are not usually traced back to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: Si S de type fini sur un corps de [nombres], ... les foncteurs de 3), mais sans filtration sur T_DR(M). Il résulterait de la conj. du double vaisseau que ce foncteur est pl. fidèle.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical attribution of the families/relative period conjecture. It also offers a route to full faithfulness over transcendental fields via spreading out, which is a strategy behind Ayoub's proof of the relative statement.

missed.claim: The name 'conjecture du double vaisseau' for the Betti/de Rham full-faithfulness conjecture seems unrecorded in the literature.
missed.quote: C'est une conséquence de la conjecture "du double vaisseau" de 4) + Tate ou Hodge
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck had an explicitly named, motivic (Hom-level) form of the period conjecture in 1965. Previously this was known only through Lang's footnote.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is fragmentary but records a named 1965 conjecture equivalent to the Grothendieck period conjecture in Hom form. It also records an explicit families version using algebraic connections without filtration. That is close to Ayoub's later relative period conjecture and is not generally credited to Grothendieck. The page has no proofs, and the reading is uncertain.
